newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria shares suspended in Vienna.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria shares suspended in Vienna.

text.p: The Vienna stock exchange said on Wednesday it had suspended trade in all Bank Austria shares and participation certificates.
A stock exchange spokesman later said by telephone the suspension was ahead of an important announcement.

Earlier, Bank Austria, Austria's biggest bank, declined comment on a newspaper report that it would offer 16 billion schillings ($1.5 billion) for rival Creditanstalt Bankverein, outdoing an existing bid.
Tabloid daily Neue Kronen Zeitung said Bank Austria's supervisory board would approve the bid for the state's 70 percent of ordinary voting shares in Creditanstalt at a meeting on Wednesday.
A spokesman for Bank Austria confirmed only that the supervisory board would meet at 1500 GMT.

On Tuesday, Creditanstalt supervisory board chief Walter Freymuth said a "serious source" had told him Bank Austria was poised to submit a bid to Finance Minister Viktor Klima by the final December 16 deadline.
Bank Austria also declined comment on Freymuth's remarks.
According to the Krone Zeitung, Bank Austria would finance the bid itself. It would continue to operate both banks, which together would rank among Europe's top 30.

A consortium headed by EA-Generali has offered 720-730 schillings a share -- a total of about 10 billion schillings -- for two thirds of the state's 19.9 million Creditanstalt ordinary shares, according to Austrian media.
At current market prices the government's stake is worth about 14 billion schillings. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254 ($ = 10.86 Austrian Schillings)
